answers.label: Q1(a)
answers.finalAnswer: 'Corona-phobia': a fear of an invisible enemy that could wipe out mankind like the dinosaurs.
answers.solution: COVID-19 has created 'corona-phobia' in our minds. It is a fear shared by the whole world, the fear of an invisible enemy that no weapon can kill and that threatens to wipe out mankind just as the dinosaurs were wiped out.

answers.label: Q1(b)
answers.finalAnswer: If people stay indoors to stay safe they starve; if they go out to earn a living they risk their lives.
answers.solution:
Mankind is caught in a dilemma. To protect ourselves from the pandemic we must stay indoors, but then we cannot earn and may starve. To earn a living we must go out to work, even at the risk of our lives.

(The passage calls this being 'caught between the devil and the deep blue sea'.)

answers.label: Q1(c)
answers.finalAnswer: Not to give in to fear; to prepare for the worst and do our duty, facing challenges bravely.
answers.solution: Soldiers prepare for the worst and never surrender to fear. They do not sit indoors thinking only of their safety; they go out and do their duty, and they prepare their minds to face every challenge. We too must face the challenges of the pandemic fearlessly, though not foolishly.

answers.label: Q1(d)
answers.finalAnswer: Face it fearlessly but sensibly, keep working, improve our immunity and learn to live with it.
answers.solution: We can deal with the pandemic by facing it fearlessly but not foolishly. We must keep working, since work is life, while taking care. Above all, we must improve our immunity and learn to live with this danger; then the enemy's days will be numbered.

answers.label: Q1(e)
answers.finalAnswer: (i) go the way of the dinosaurs; (ii) take the bull by the horns; (iii) caught between the devil and the deep blue sea
answers.solution:
(i) to become extinct: **go the way of the dinosaurs**
(ii) to face a difficulty bravely: **take the bull by the horns**
(iii) be in a dilemma: **(be) caught between the devil and the deep blue sea**

answers.label: Q1(f)
answers.finalAnswer: No. It respects no man-made barriers like caste, colour, ethnicity or religion; it affects everyone alike.
answers.solution: No, the pandemic is not partial. It has no respect for man-made barriers such as caste, colour, ethnicity or religion, and it can attack anyone. That is why the whole world is united by 'corona-phobia'.

answers.label: Q1(g)
answers.finalAnswer: Do not give in to fear; like soldiers, face the pandemic bravely but sensibly, keep working, build immunity and learn to live with it.
answers.solution: The passage tells us not to surrender to fear. Like soldiers, we should face the pandemic bravely but sensibly, carry on with our work, improve our immunity and learn to live with the disease. Then we can defeat it.

answers.label: Q.2(a)
answers.finalAnswer: The Fearless Little Rabbit
answers.solution: A suitable title: **The Fearless Little Rabbit** (or 'I Am Not Afraid'). The poem is about a little rabbit who refuses to live in fear.

answers.label: Q.2(b)
answers.finalAnswer: Repetition
answers.solution: **Repetition**: the line 'My parents tell me not to go out' and the word 'Therefore, I'm not afraid' are repeated in each stanza. (Personification is also used: the rabbit speaks like a person, and 'destiny has its own plans'.)

answers.label: Q.2(c)
answers.finalAnswer: To stay at home, not go out, and obey them so that it stays safe and becomes successful.
answers.solution: The parents want the little rabbit to stay at home and not go out, because it could be killed by a big animal, carried away by a big bird, or fall ill or get hurt. They want it to obey them so that it will be safe and successful in future.

answers.label: Q.2(d)
answers.finalAnswer: Fearless and carefree; it accepts nature and destiny, loves playing with friends and lives for the present.
answers.solution: The rabbit is fearless and lives for the present. It accepts that it is part of nature's food chain and that destiny has its own plans, so it is not afraid of tigers, eagles, illness or injury. It loves playing with its friends and feels that 'now' is what matters.

answers.label: Q.2(e)
answers.finalAnswer: The parents scold the rabbit angrily, but their anger comes from love and worry for its safety.
answers.solution: The line means that the parents speak sharply, even angrily, because the rabbit does not listen to them. But their anger comes from love: they are worried about its safety and want it to be safe and successful.

answers.label: Q.2(f)
answers.finalAnswer: Do not let fear stop you from living and enjoying the present.
answers.solution: The moral of the poem is that we should not let fear stop us from living. Dangers are always there, but we must enjoy the present moment with courage, while still loving and respecting our parents.

answers.label: Q.3
answers.finalAnswer: Precis titled 'Education Turns Uniqueness into Talent'.
answers.solution:
**Title: Education Turns Uniqueness into Talent**

Great thinkers have defined education in many ways, but all agree that it teaches us valuable lessons about life. It widens our outlook and shows us our abilities and our duties as citizens. Its main aim is to bring out the best in a person. Since every person is unique, good education must discover each child's special quality and help it grow into a talent. Neglected, the same quality may turn into a vice.

(77 words)

answers.label: Q.4
answers.finalAnswer: Two essays: (a) Genius is an infinite capacity for taking pains; (b) Technology is making us unsocial.
answers.solution:
Topics chosen: (a) and (b).

**(a) Genius is an Infinite Capacity for Taking Pains**

Many people believe that a genius is born with special gifts and succeeds without effort. This is not true. Behind every great achievement lie years of hard work, patience and practice.

Thomas Edison failed hundreds of times before he made a working electric bulb. He said that genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration. Sachin Tendulkar practised for hours every day from childhood before he became a great batsman. Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam studied late into the night under a lamp.

Talent is only a seed. It grows into genius only when it is watered with effort and patience. A person who is ready to work hard, learn from mistakes and never give up can achieve wonderful things.

So, as students, we should not wait for luck. We should take pains, work steadily and keep improving. That is the real secret of genius.

**(b) Technology is Making Us Unsocial**

Technology has made our lives easier. With a mobile phone we can talk to anyone in the world, study online and shop from home. But it has also made many of us unsocial.

Today, family members sit in the same room, but each one is busy with a phone. Children prefer video games to playing outdoors with friends. People have hundreds of 'friends' on social media but hardly anyone to talk to face to face. We send a birthday message instead of visiting a friend. Slowly, we are losing the warmth of real relationships.

Technology itself is not bad. The problem is that we use it too much. We should fix screen time, keep phones away during meals and spend time with family and friends.

If we use technology wisely, it can bring people closer instead of keeping them apart.

answers.label: Q.5
answers.finalAnswer: Story with title about boarding the wrong train and losing a wallet on the way to an interview in Mumbai.
answers.solution:
**A Journey I Will Never Forget**

Last year, I had to go to Mumbai by train to attend an important job interview. I left home early, but on the way my taxi got stuck in a long traffic jam. By the time I reached the railway station, my train was about to leave.

In a hurry, I jumped into a train on the platform without checking its name. After some time, I asked a fellow passenger when we would reach Mumbai. He laughed and said the train was going to Chennai! I was shocked. When I reached for my ticket, I found that my wallet was missing too. I had lost it in the rush at the station.

I got down at the next station, feeling helpless. A kind station master listened to my story, helped me call my family and put me on a train to Mumbai. I reached late, but the company gave me another date.

Now I always check the train and keep my wallet safe. Haste really does make waste.

answers.label: Q.6
answers.finalAnswer: Letter to a friend describing the school Annual Day, the writer's role, and how the friend was missed.
answers.solution:
Room 12, Tagore House
Rashtriya Indian Military College
Dehradun
15 June 2020

Dear Rohan,

I hope you are enjoying your stay at your grandparents' home. I am writing to tell you about our school's Annual Day, which was held last Saturday.

The function was a grand success. The chief guest was a retired Army general. The programme began with the school song, followed by a dance, a skit and the prize distribution. I was the compere of the evening, and I also played the role of Shivaji in our house play. At first I was nervous, but everyone praised my performance and the chief guest shook my hand.

I missed you a lot, Rohan. You are the best singer in our class, and our choir did not sound the same without you. Everyone asked about you.

Come back soon. I will show you all the photographs.

Yours lovingly,
Aman

answers.label: Q.7
answers.finalAnswer: 'For' the statement: social media causes more harm than good.
answers.solution:
**For the motion: Social Media Causes More Harm than Good**

Social media like Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp were made to connect people, but today they cause more harm than good.

First, social media is addictive. Students spend hours scrolling, which wastes time meant for study, sleep and exercise. Second, it spreads fake news and rumours very quickly, which can create fear and even violence. Third, many young people compare their lives with the perfect pictures they see online and feel sad, jealous or lonely. Cyberbullying and online fraud are also growing.

It is true that social media helps us share information and keep in touch with friends. But these benefits are small compared with the damage it does to our health, our studies and our relationships.

Therefore, I strongly believe that social media causes more harm than good, and we must use it with great care and limits.

answers.label: Q.8
answers.finalAnswer: (a) Claustrophobia; (b) Encyclopaedia; (c) Pandemic; (d) Swarm; (e) Utopia
answers.solution:
(a) Fear of confined places: **Claustrophobia**
(b) A book that contains information on various subjects: **Encyclopaedia**
(c) A disease which spreads over a wide geographical area in a large proportion of the population: **Pandemic**
(d) A large group of insects moving in a mass: **Swarm**
(e) An imaginary ideal society free of poverty and suffering: **Utopia**

answers.label: Q.9
answers.finalAnswer: (i) the; (ii) the; (iii) Ø; (iv) an; (v) Ø; (vi) a; (vii) the; (viii) a; (ix) a; (x) The; (xi) Ø; (xii) the; (xiii) the; (xiv) The; (xv) Ø; (xvi) the; (xvii) Ø; (xviii) Ø; (xix) a; (xx) a
answers.solution:
(a) Moving to (i) **the** United States was (ii) **the** most exciting thing I have ever done. I moved last year to (iii) **Ø** New York. New York is (iv) **an** exciting city, full of (v) **Ø** adventure. In fact, I saw (vi) **a** famous actor on (vii) **the** street yesterday!
(b) Today I have (viii) **a** job interview at (ix) **a** financial company. (x) **The** company has (xi) **Ø** offices all over (xii) **the** world. I'm not sure that I have (xiii) **the** skills to get hired. I hope so. (xiv) **The** company's office is on (xv) **Ø** Main Street. That's (xvi) **the** same street my friend works on.
(c) If I get hired, I could meet him after (xvii) **Ø** work for drinks. That would be great. He's from (xviii) **Ø** Scotland. He works 8 hours (xix) **a** day, 5 days (xx) **a** week.

Rules used: 'the' with a plural country name, superlatives, things already mentioned and 'the world'/'the same'; no article with most city, street and country names or with uncountable nouns used generally; 'a' for 'per' (8 hours a day).

answers.label: Q.11
answers.finalAnswer: (a) (i) banking on; (b) (iii) bear out; (c) (ii) call upon; (d) (i) break up; (e) (iv) taken aback; (f) (ii) asking for
answers.solution:
(a) She is **banking on** the bank loan for her higher studies. (depending on)
(b) Modern researches **bear out** that yoga cures diseases. (confirm)
(c) Many people **call upon** God for help rather than to thank him. (appeal to)
(d) The police were called in to **break up** the rioters. (scatter)
(e) I was **taken aback** when I topped the merit list. (surprised)
(f) He is **asking for** trouble if he quarrels with the house owner. (inviting)

Note on (c): as printed, the sentence reads 'call ... to God', and both (ii) 'call upon' and (iv) 'call on' can mean 'appeal to'; 'call upon' is the better fit for a prayer for help.

answers.finalAnswer: (a) She asked whether she needed to write a letter.; (b) Raj is better than most other boys in the class.; (c) It is known to everyone that he is a rich man.; (d) This news can never be true.; (e) Eating more than necessary makes one fat.; (f) Did I not tell you to work hard?; (g) She was very gentle in explaining her point of view.; (h) He forced his way through the crowd.; (j) He never failed in anything he attempted.; (k) Taking off his clothes, he plunged into the river.
answers.solution:
(a) She asked whether she needed to write a letter.
(b) Raj is better than most other boys in the class.
(c) It is known to everyone that he is a rich man.
(d) This news can never be true.
(e) Eating more than necessary makes one fat. (or: Overeating makes one fat.)
(f) Did I not tell you to work hard?
(g) She was very gentle in explaining her point of view. ('gently' becomes the adjective 'gentle')
(h) He forced his way through the crowd. ('forcibly' becomes the verb 'forced')
(j) He never failed in anything he attempted.
(k) Taking off his clothes, he plunged into the river.

Note: as printed, no word is underlined in (g); the only sensible word is 'gently'. The parts also skip label (i).

answers.label: Q.14
answers.finalAnswer: (a) (iv) with; (b) (ii) to; (c) (iv) no preposition needed; (d) (ii) with; (e) (ii) of; (f) (ii) on; (g) (ii) to, by
answers.solution:
(a) Tagore was endowed **with** rare talents.
(b) You are not amenable **to** reason.
(c) He emphasised his point. ('emphasise' takes a direct object; no preposition)
(d) I beg to differ **with** you on this subject.
(e) The poor old man was blind **of** one eye. (the traditional textbook usage; 'blind in one eye' is also common today)
(f) My friend insisted **on** my staying with her a little longer.
(g) Entry **to** this auditorium is **by** ticket.
